overview: Both involve the immune system overreacting, but autoimmunity targets the body's own cells while allergy overreacts to a harmless external substance.
genZNote: Autoimmunity: the immune system turning on its own team. Allergy: the immune system massively overreacting to something totally harmless.

aspects.label: What's Targeted
aspects.valueA: The body's own healthy cells and tissues (self-antigens).
aspects.valueB: A normally harmless external substance (allergen) like pollen or dust.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueB: Hay fever, food allergies, asthma triggered by allergens.

aspects.label: Underlying Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Failure of self-tolerance — the immune system fails to distinguish self from non-self.
aspects.valueB: An exaggerated (hypersensitivity) response to a normally non-threatening antigen.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Allergy is technically classified as Type I hypersensitivity, mediated by IgE — a direct link back to that immunoglobulin comparison.
overlay.memoryTrick: Autoimmunity = attacking 'self'. Allergy = overreacting to something harmless from 'outside'.
overlay.commonMisconception: Allergy is not the same thing as a normal immune response to infection — it's specifically an inappropriate, exaggerated reaction to something that poses no real threat.
